content.text:
I submitted index 5 (Bi 0.41, Cu 0.19, V 0.40) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent I measured, 1.06×10⁻⁵ A, but with only 3 of the 149 compositions measured, I can't confirm it's the best in the library.

I used all 3 photocurrent measurements:

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| **5** | 0.41 / 0.19 / 0.40 | **1.06×10⁻⁵** |
| 8 | 0.46 / 0.21 / 0.33 | 6.1×10⁻⁶ |
| 89 | 0.04 / 0.58 / 0.38 | 1.4×10⁻⁷ |

- **Why index 5 first:** it has the least copper in the library and roughly equal bismuth and vanadium, so it's the closest match to bismuth vanadate (BiVO₄), the best-known photoanode in this system.
- **Index 89:** I measured it to check the copper–vanadium-rich region. Its photocurrent was about 75 times lower, so that region is poor.
- **Index 8:** a bismuth-rich composition near index 5, ranked highly by the Gaussian-process suggestion tool. It came in lower than index 5.

The results suggest photocurrent rises as the composition gets closer to BiVO₄ and falls as copper increases, but three data points are too few to be sure. I didn't use any of the 5 X-ray diffraction measurements, so the crystal phases present were never confirmed.
